payload.description: Loop deficiency: a dev session named its story spec <id>.md instead of <id>-<slug>.md (story 21-6). bmad-loop v0.9.1 resolves a spec by the glob <id>-*.md, so it read the finished, committed story as pending, logged a result-less Stop (verdict pending) and armed the stall grace. Closed by hand: git mv to <id>-<slug>.md and a commit. Hole to plug: the studio customization (bmad-build-auto.toml) or the manifest's invoke_dev_with should pin the spec file name, and the pre_commit gate should refuse a stories/ file that does not match <id>-*.md.

Loop deficiency: Claude Code 2.1.283 showed the dialog 'Make auto mode your default permission mode?' inside a bmad-loop dev session started with --permission-mode bypassPermissions. The engine's stall nudge was typed into that dialog, which answered it: the sandbox's ~/.claude/settings.json gained permissions.defaultMode=auto at 21:11:02Z and the live session switched to auto mode. The nudge text never reached the agent. Hole to plug: provision-engine.sh should pre-answer the dialog in the sandbox's user settings, and the runbook should name the setting.

Loop deficiency (bmad-loop v0.9.1, upstream candidate): the dev-stall grace re-arms on any growth of the tee'd pane log, and Claude Code's rotating footer tips grow that log while the session is idle. After the first stall nudge the second one never fired (stall_nudges_sent stayed 1 for 14+ minutes), so session_timeout_min was the only bound on an idle finished session.

Loop deficiency: the supervisor's machine-local policy.toml keeps the engine template's max_tokens_per_story=2000000, while every Opus 5.5 story measured 3.9M to 4.4M weighted tokens (21-4: 3.86M, 21-5: 4.40M). Each story journals token-budget-exceeded. kb/execution-pipeline-model-routing.md records 5000000 as the value that held. Hole to plug: tk-studio-launch or pipeline.py apply should check the policy limits against the budget bands and report a mismatch.

Loop deficiency: an sbx engine reads the Windows host checkout, where files under '* text=auto' are CRLF. TUA's verify gate was red on 2 of 1030 tests (golden .tss compared on LF) in the sandbox and would be on the host; the main PC's WSL clone is LF and hid it. Fixed per project by pinning the format to LF (the-universe-awaits PR #2). Hole to plug: tk-studio onboarding or activate should report text formats a project's tests read byte-exact that are not pinned to LF when the project has an sbx engine.

Loop deficiency: story spec files are named <id>-<slug>.md where the id already carries the title slug, so names reach about 150 characters. A clone of the supervisor under a deep folder fails on Windows with 'Filename too long' (MAX_PATH); host verification needs a short-path clone such as «path»<name>. Hole to plug: the task-planning instructions could use short ids (21-6) for file names, or the runbook could set core.longpaths.

payload.description: Loop deficiency: story 21-5 landed with a race in its signal path (handlers installed after spawn() returned), and its own signal tests passed at its gate by timing. One story later the same tests were red in the engine on every run, the 21-6 review session could not find the cause, consult ruled escalate, and the run paused. Closed by hand: root cause found with timing marks in a scratch copy, fixed in 76ded1b with a test that fails 15 of 15 on the old code. Hole to plug: the verify gate should run process and signal tests more than once (or under a repeat flag) before a story lands, and the consult instructions should name 'run the failing test N times on the baseline and record the failure rate' as the first step on verify-red.

Loop deficiency: when a run pauses on an escalation after the story's work is committed, the engine's close-out never runs: no studio gate (reconcile), no post_commit meter, no follow-up-review deferral, no squash. Closing story 21-6 by hand took seven steps (commit the pending pass, fix, verify on both hosts, spec status and resolution, reconcile and replan notes, meter from the run dir, trial data and archive). Hole to plug: a studio script or tk-studio-launch verb that closes a landed story by hand in one step, from the runbook's 'when a run pauses' list.

Loop deficiency: a headless tk-studio-launch session (epic-22-launch1, Opus 5.5) wrote SPEC.md, met the dirty tree at its second readiness check, and ended by asking the operator for permission to commit. It printed no status block (AD-11: never a question, always the block). The Epic 24 launch committed its own bootstrap; the Epic 20 launch ended blocked. Three launches, three behaviours. Hole to plug: tk-studio-launch should state one rule for its own bootstrap output (commit it on the run branch, then re-check), and conformance should drive the dirty-tree case.

Loop deficiency: story 22-2 landed with a test that fails only on Windows (test/page.test.ts expects '~/planted-home-file'; on win32 the page shows '~\planted-home-file'). The engine's gate runs on Linux only, so it was green. The Windows host run after the story caught it; the product behaviour is right and the fix is one line in the test. Third Windows-only finding after the canonicalPath case fold (21-4) and DW-5. Hole to plug: a Windows leg in the verify gate, for example the supervisor's host tier running 'bun test' in a clone of the story commit before the story is accepted.

Loop deficiency: story 22-3 enabled the end-to-end suites on win32 and wrote their win32 paths from Linux, where they cannot run. The first Windows host run failed 29 of 548 tests. Every cause was test-side: .cmd fakes cannot be spawned without a shell (EINVAL), a killed process reports exit code 1 not SIGKILL, bun's folder also holds uv under WinGet, symlinks need a privilege, and the fake sbx used the VM folder as a host folder. Closed by hand in 39596da (no production change); the host is 545 pass, 16 skip, 0 fail. Hole to plug: the same Windows leg as the verify gate needs; a story that touches win32 paths cannot be accepted on a Linux run alone.

payload.description: Loop deficiency: Story 28.2's nearest-root rule excluded only the configured per-user store (TK_STUDIO_HOME) from being a project root, so with that variable set (every test, every supervisor worker) the default ~/.tk-studio/config.yaml still counted, and on Windows, where %TEMP% and every project under the profile sit below ~, «path» resolved as the project root for all of them: 17 failures and 2 errors in the lib suite and one conformance drive red on the host gate, while the Linux engine was green (/tmp is outside HOME). A real product bug on any Windows box, not only a test artifact. Closed by hand on loop/epic-28: a .tk-studio/ holding a store-only folder (registry/, measurements/, projects/) or matching the configured or default store root is a store, never a project; a test reproduces it on every OS. Hole to plug: the engine's Linux-only view keeps missing path-layout defects (holes 11/12/22 again); until the host-verify leg runs on every tk-studio run (Story 27.4 through the supervisor, 28.3/28.4), the hand-launch recipe must run tools/verify_host.py before any PR, and the planner should flag every rule that walks the filesystem upward as a Windows-profile case.

Closed by hand on loop/epic-28: a fallback shim on symlink failure (each tool's own folder on PATH, a tool sharing a folder with bun or bmad-loop copied into the shim), plus three host-only fixture fixes (core.longpaths in the isolated gitconfig on Windows, shlex-quoted paths in a report assertion, an existing live file as a 'never written' probe).
